reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or activation levels in systems, we often need a function that maps any real number to a bounded range between zero and one. The logistic function achieves this by placing the input inside an exponential denominator. As the input grows very large, the denominator dominates and the output approaches one. As the input drops to large negative values, the exponential vanishes and the output falls to zero. The steepness parameter scales how fast this transition occurs, while the midpoint shifts the center of the curve.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any real number into the range between zero and one. Adjust the steepness $k$ and midpoint $x_0$ to see how the S-curve bends.
reply.instructions: Adjust the sliders for steepness and midpoint to change the curve. Observe how the output and slope update at the marker.
